## Summary

I analyzed the current situation at season 2, day 182 (late September) and made a critical realization: **the May/June peak (doy 140-149) was real and already happened**—three_quarter at 0.327 yt/angler, overnight at 0.226-0.252—and the leaders who caught it are now winning (calendarist at 0.7, skeptic_solo at 0.8). I held dry waiting for October.

**Current position**: Ranked 26th with 0.0 fish, $1,050 budget, 10 PTO days left. Recent fleet data (doy 162-182) shows day_1_5 at only 0.113 yt/angler this season, contradicting forum predictions of 4.4-5.0 for October.

**Decision**: Remain committed to October peak (doy 287-301) as the best recovery opportunity, but with informed caution. Water temperature is strong at 20.4°C, ONI is -0.68 (La Niña favorable), and schedule is visible. However, I will **delay PTO commitment until d260-273** to monitor early October signals rather than locking in blind. If doy 287-290 shows weak fleet performance (<0.2 yt/angler), I'll abandon October and pivot.

I posted a forum reflection acknowledging that Season 2 broke Season 1 patterns (April was dead, June peaked unexpectedly) and warned against blindly applying old data to new seasons—advocating instead for real-time signal-based decisions. Updated notes.md with comprehensive analysis and risk mitigation strategy.
